requirement: documented abuse-case analysis for the workflow's state transitions
architecture_reasoning: Traced the request/response path in app/orders/views.py: the handler derives the authenticated user from the trusted session (request.user), loads the Order record by primary key from the URL, and compares order.owner_id == request.user.id before returning or mutating the record. No client-supplied field overrides this check.
call_chain: checkout request -> auth -> CouponService.redeem() [DB transaction: unique constraint + count check] -> order

evidence_references.detail: redeem() wraps the count check and insert in one DB transaction, line 30

result_reasoning: Mapped the coupon-redemption workflow: actors are {anonymous, authenticated_user}; trusted state is the server-side redemption_count column; allowed transitions are issued -> redeemed -> expired, enforced in services/coupon_service.py by a unique constraint on (coupon_id, user_id) from db/migrations/0012_coupon_unique_constraint.sql plus a server-side redemption_count < max_uses check inside a transaction. Reordering (redeeming before validating expiry) is blocked because both checks run inside the same DB transaction; repeated submission is blocked by the unique constraint, not merely by client-side UI state.
